newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan delays stock futures trading - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan delays stock futures trading - paper.

text.p: Taiwan planned to begin allowing local trading of offshore Taiwan stock-index futures in Chicago and Singapore on August 1 after postponing the expected start from June 1, local media reported on Wednesday.
Officials from the Securities and Futures Commission were not available immediately for confirmation.

The Economic Daily News said commission chairman Lu Daung-yen told futures traders on Monday that trading of offshore stock-index futures had to be delayed until August 1 due to inadequate staffing to handle the new trading.

Under the liberalisation, Taiwan futures houses for the first time will be allowed to trade futures linked to Taiwan's stock market performance that are offered by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) and Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX).

The CME and SIMEX launched the contracts on January 9 over the objections of Taiwan market regulators, who had asked for them to wait until Taipei could open its own futures market and launch its own stock index contracts.

Under a Futures Trading Law enacted by parliament in early March after years of delays, the Taiwan exchange could open no sooner than October -- giving SIMEX and CME a head-start of several months to attract Taiwan investors.
Singapore traders and analysts have said SIMEX would benefit most from Taiwan's liberalisation. Some local traders said the CME may give up the Taiwan market if trading volume remained small.
